title: decision records cannot express who ruled, what a ruling binds, what it excludes, or supersession -- opum-doc built a separate grants/*.json store because the tracker record had nowhere for that
description:
Raised by opum-agent (OPAG-199, 2026-09-18, dispatched at 12:44Z with the user's approval), relayed by this session and filed on its own judgment about scope.

`quest decision` (quest help decision) carries only title, context, outcome, status -- no field for who made the ruling, under what authority, what the ruling binds, what it explicitly does NOT cover, or what it supersedes. opum-agent points to opum-doc's grants/*.json store (docs/reference/opum-fleet-permission-grants.md, grants/schema.json) as the worked example: it grew a second, schema-validated JSON store specifically because authority + scope + expiry + revocation had nowhere to live in a tracker record. Read directly (not taken on relay) before filing this: the grants schema models grantee{kind,identifier}, scope[] (enumerated, no wildcard), resources[] (no wildcard), granted_by, granted_at, expires_at (required, no "forever"), and revoked{status,revoked_by,revoked_at} enforced together by a conditional schema rule.

A second signal opum-agent supplied: opum-agent itself has recorded ZERO quest decisions while making rulings constantly -- evidence the current shape is not getting used for what it exists for, not just a taste preference.

This is NOT a request to copy the grants schema verbatim -- grants encode authorization for irreversible/permission-gated actions with hard expiry; decisions encode a ruling's reasoning and scope, which does not need to expire the same way. Read it for the shape of the gap (authority, scope, exclusion, supersession as first-class fields), not as a template to clone.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A concrete field model is proposed for quest decision covering: who ruled (an actor/authority field, distinct from the generic --actor on every write), what the ruling binds (a scope, analogous to grants scope[]/resources[]), what it explicitly excludes, and what it supersedes (a link to a prior decision id)
The proposal states explicitly what it does NOT borrow from opum-doc grants/schema.json and why -- expiry/revocation are a poor fit for a ruling record and should not be copied by default
quest manifest --json and quest help decision document any new fields
A migration/backfill stance is decided for existing decision records missing the new fields (leave them, or infer supersession from context) and stated in the task notes
opum-agent's stated signal -- zero decisions recorded there despite frequent rulings -- is referenced when judging whether the new shape is actually easier to use, not just more complete
